o: An employee is high-access if some 3 of their access times fit within a window strictly shorter than 60 minutes (same day, so no wraparound). Convert 'HHMM' to minutes, sort each employee's times, and check whether any times[i+2] − times[i] < 60. Example 1: 'a' has 05:32, 05:49, 06:21 — span 49 < 60 → high-access.
k: Three times within an hour ⟺ min gap over consecutive triples < 60 after sorting.
Convert HHMM to absolute minutes to make comparisons trivial.

a.n: Approach 1: Sort per employee + triple scan
a.i: Sorting puts the closest triple adjacent; a sliding check of every consecutive triple suffices.
s: Bucket times by employee as minutes
a.t: O(N log N) for sorting all timestamps

a.n: Approach 2: Fixed-size sliding window per employee
a.i: Instead of checking triples, maintain a window of times within 60 minutes of the current time and count entries — equivalent logic phrased as a two-pointer sweep.
s: Two pointers: advance right, shrink left while diff ≥ 60
High-access if window size ≥ 3 at any point

w: Both are equally fine; the triple check is shorter. Pitfalls: exactly-one-hour-apart times must NOT count (use strict < 60), and parsing '0549' as an integer directly (549) breaks comparisons — split hours/minutes. Duplicate timestamps are allowed and count multiple times.
